checks: The convex hull is compact by grouping the finitely many compact generating fibers with a coefficient simplex. At zero there is a full-dimensional continuous fiber, and the projected vertices span the base space, so the full lifted hull has dimension n+d.

Each projected vertex is exposed. A combination over an edge midpoint stays within its edge by the face property, and its three possible generating fibers are all subsets of D because 0∈D and the shrink ratio is in (0,1). The full D at the midpoint proves equality there.

All integer bases are exactly zero, 2e_i, e_i and e_i+e_j for distinct i,j. The volumes are one at zero and every edge midpoint, and 1/3 at the other n vertices. Each augmented edge term is 3(1+1/3)/4=1. Summation gives (3N²−N+4)/6, including N=2.
For n=2 the sum is 14/3, so M/4−B=7/6−1=1/6. The source comparison concerns the displayed scalar certificate only, with no upper bound on true depth.
Original 0e12a7390f0ce25f §4, equation (6), is the same actual homothetic witness and the same arithmetic n=2 specialization.

overlap.comparison: Its calibration includes constant-volume products over a dilated simplex for residue-level expansion. The present construction has unit midpoint volumes and unequal vertex volumes, and realizes a different scalar objective.

readability: Sharpness of the universal numerical inequality is the separately reviewed complete-graph result. This construction computes the matching value exactly as a standalone witness.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen proof, then original-source and accepted-predecessor comparison.
summary: The specified lifted convex hull realizes the sharp numerical menu exactly and gives the stated n=2 shortfall of its scalar certificate.
